prayerExcerpt.en-US: As he hung upon the cross, Jesus said to the disciple whom he loved: Behold your mother.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Pendente da cruz, disse Jesus ao discípulo que ele amava: Eis a tua mãe!

meta.face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md, the same face matured (the same woman, not a different face), a woman of about forty-eight with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head; eyes lowered in sorrow and trust. St. John as in recurring-figures.md: a beardless young man of about twenty-two with a smooth OVAL face, large upturned brown eyes, a straight nose, a small full mouth; wavy golden-brown hair to the jaw; a green tunic and a red-orange mantle; he looks at her with devotion. The two must read as clearly different: she mature, veiled, in blue; he beardless and golden-haired, in green and red-orange.
meta.basis: The feast's Mass is built on John 19:25-27 (gospel, collect, communion antiphon): at the Cross Christ gave his Mother to the beloved disciple, and in him to the Church. The Cenacle of Acts 1:14 was passed over because the pentecost card already shows Our Lady among the Apostles. Faces from recurring-figures.md.

sources.title: Congregation for Divine Worship, Decree on the memorial of Mary Mother of the Church (2018)
